title: 1975 AHSME Problem 11
statement: Let \(P\) be an interior point of circle \(K\) other than the center of \(K.\) Form all chords of \(K\) which pass through \(P,\) and determine their midpoints. The locus of these midpoints is

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text: a circle with one point deleted

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text:
a circle if the distance from \(P\) to the center of \(K\) is
less than one half the radius of \(K;\) otherwise a circular arc of
less than \(360^\circ\)

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text: a semicircle with one point deleted

solutions.text:
If \(M\) is a chord midpoint and \(O\) is the center, then \(OM\) is perpendicular to the chord, so \(\angle OMP=90^\circ\) unless \(M=O.\) Thus \(M\) lies on the circle with diameter \(OP.\) Conversely, each nonendpoint \(M\) on that circle gives \(PM\perp OM,\) so the line \(PM\) cuts a chord of \(K\) whose midpoint is \(M.\) The endpoint \(M=P\) gives the chord through \(P\) perpendicular to \(OP,\) while \(M=O\) gives the diameter through \(O\) and \(P.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: Join a chord midpoint \(M\) to the circle’s center \(O\)
Since \(OM\) is perpendicular to the chord through \(P,\) \(\angle OMP=90^\circ\)
